scope: User-requested CPU-only validation of project-rule removal, immutable recovery archives, restoration and lock freshness; separate from the completed model study.

scenarios.roundtrip: Remove the active rule, retain its complete archive, observe stale lock, refresh the inactive-rule lock, restore the original rule, observe stale lock again, refuse a duplicate restore, then refresh the lock.
scenarios.conflict: With a different active rule under the original ID, refuse restoration with exit 2 and preserve the active rules, recovery archive, manifest, configuration and experiment code.
scenarios.tampered: On an isolated controlled copy with a preserved original archive, change the archive reason without updating its content ID. Refuse restoration with exit 2 and preserve both the damaged copy and current rules.

acceptance: Use the actual pinned source CLI in isolated committed CPU fixtures, with a runtime import witness and independent package-file identity verification. Keep installed packages unchanged.

Preserve ID, field, severity, original reason, source, optional candidate ID, approval timestamp and all CLI/config/environment bindings semantically. The contract does not promise original YAML formatting.
Independently recompute each recovery archive content ID according to specification section 7.2. A recovery archive is not by itself evidence that removal completed.
Exercise CLI, config and environment observations for the same declared synthetic defense value. The recorder consumption field remains unverified.

For roundtrip, compare lock bytes before and after freshness checks. Refresh while the rule is inactive before testing restored-rule staleness; restoration to the original rules may legitimately match an older lock.
Derive expected input changes from independent before/after byte inventories. Pre/post capture is not continuous monitoring: transient changes restored before the final check may not be visible.
Keep per-command arguments, actual/expected exits and normalized public output with original output digests. Expected inner CLI refusals do not require the outer validation driver to fail.
Retain original recorder directories, selected-run exports, independent intermediate rule/lock snapshots and archive backups. Inspection and expected refusals must not rewrite captured history.
Probe released CLI capabilities explicitly; unavailable source-only commands are not failed released-product behavior.

All existing scientific inputs, model-response accounting and prior records remain unchanged. Publish only reviewed portable fixture data; retain machine paths and private configuration outside the public repository.
limits: No model inference, paid endpoint, discovery model call, resource qualification or cross-process concurrency guarantee.
The tampered archive is deliberately constructed; no real data loss, power failure or malicious credential extraction is tested.
This is one consumer project; a product change or upstream Issue/PR requires a concrete reproducible defect or reusable improvement.
